subject: DPA onboarding: Kestrel Health — subprocessors, transfers, and e-sign pathway
messages:
From: Anna Bryant <anna.bryant@kestrelhealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@kestrelhealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Initial DPA request & subprocessor disclosure — Kestrel Health onboarding

Hi Michael,

We’re getting close to the onboarding window for the pilot and legal has asked us to collect the following before we move to PO: an initial DPA (your template if available), the list of subprocessors with locations, and confirmation of how Redwood handles cross-border transfers (EU -> US egress / SCCs / UK addendum).

Two specific asks from our side:
- Can you share a DPA template we can circulate to our counsel?
- Do you have an e-sign preference (DocuSign vs AdobeSign) and can you confirm whether you will execute under SCCs or a UK addendum if required?

Also: our security team is sensitive to any unattended cloud egress to non-EU regions — please flag which subprocessors may have data residency or egress implications.

Appreciate a short packet (DPA + subprocessor list + preferred signing flow). Hope to close intake this week.

Thanks,
Anna Bryant
Head of Integrations
Kestrel Health

Attachment: procurement_onboarding_checklist.pdf (referenced)

From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
To: Anna Bryant <anna.bryant@kestrelhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial DPA request & subprocessor disclosure — Kestrel Health onboarding

Hi Anna — thanks for the clear list. Attaching our current DPA template and the canonical subprocessor list. Quick notes up front:

- Attachment: Redwood_DPA_v1.2.docx (template) and subprocessor_list_2026.csv (exported list) are attached.
- E-sign: we default to DocuSign but can route via AdobeSign if you require it. Both are acceptable and we can set the envelope sender to either Redwood or Kestrel.
- Transfers: we support SCCs for EU transfers and can include the UK Addendum where required. If you need an executed SCC record, our legal ops can append the standard annex.
- Subprocessors with potential egress: highlighted in the CSV (GCP us-central for backups; audit logs routed to a third-party analytics provider in the US). We can offer EU-only retention/backups on Dedicated or Private deployments, but not for Hosted at this time.

Lauren and Stephanie are on the thread to confirm language and to surface attestation docs. If you can tell us: (1) whether you require SCCs in execution or prefer an annex, and (2) who signs on your side (name + email), we’ll prepare a DocuSign envelope and a short redline window.

Proposed timeline: 24–48h review by Redwood legal, then DocuSign envelope for signature.

Best,
Michael Grant
Head of Partnerships — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v1.2.docx, subprocessor_list_2026.csv

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Anna Bryant <anna.bryant@kestrelhealth.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial DPA request & subprocessor disclosure — Kestrel Health onboarding

Thanks, Michael. Anna — quick technical/legal clarifications from our privacy team (copied):

1) Subprocessors: the CSV lists primary subprocessors and region. Short summary: AWS (eu-west-1 for serving), GCP (eu-west-4 for model training snapshots; us-central for backups), Databrick-Analytics (US) for aggregated usage metrics, and HashiCorp Vault partner (EU primary, US secondary for failover). We can provide a signed subprocessor attestation for the current list — attached.

2) Transfers & controls: we can execute SCCs as the primary legal mechanism. If you require the UK Addendum, we’ll include it. For Hosted customers who require strict EU residency, we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private deployment; we can document the tradeoffs (cost, lead time).

3) E-sign & path: DocuSign is preferred for speed. We will prepare an envelope that includes (a) DPA, (b) executed SCC Annex (if you request), and (c) the subprocessor attestation. If you prefer AdobeSign, please confirm.

4) Redlines: if Kestrel legal returns changes to Article 5 (Transfers) or Article 9 (Subprocessors), we ask for consolidated redlines via one PDF or DocuSign markup to speed review.

Attached: subprocessor_attestation.pdf.

Proposed internal SLA on our side: Redwood legal provides a redline response within 48 hours of receiving consolidated comments. If any change impacts hosting guarantees we will escalate.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Privacy Lead — Redwood Inference

Attachment: subprocessor_attestation.pdf

From: Anna Bryant <anna.bryant@kestrelhealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@kestrelhealth.com
Date: Fri, 12 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial DPA request & subprocessor disclosure — Kestrel Health onboarding

Michael / Lauren — thanks for the quick packet and the attestation. Procurement confirms they prefer DocuSign and requests SCCs be relied on for EU data transfers. Our signatory will be: Priya Shah <pshah@kestrelhealth.com>.

We will consolidate redlines: our counsel has one change request on Clause 5.2 (narrow the permitted export for backups) and a minor clarification on notification timing for new subprocessors. We’ll return consolidated PDF by EOD Monday.

Please prepare a DocuSign envelope addressed to Priya Shah and mark the envelope for signature by Redwood first, then Kestrel. If SCC Annex needs to be appended after redlines, include the placeholder so we can see the structure.

Thanks again — aiming to have everything signed before the end of next week.

Best,
Anna Bryant
Head of Integrations
Kestrel Health
